To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in atherosclerosis, impaired efferocytotic clearance of apoptotic cells and necrotic debris leads to plaque destabilization, while in the post-MI heart, impaired efferocytoic clearance is associated with adverse cardiac remodeling and heart failure.

the resolution of inflammation in atherosclerrotic plaques is impaired by a defect in efferocytotic clearance and that this is associated with increased risk for plaque destabilization and thrombosis, while the resolution of inflammation post MI is enhanced by efferocytotically cleared necrotic debris and is associated with decreased risk for adverse cardiac remodeling.
the resolution of inflammation is impaired in atherosclerosis, but not post MI, and that the impaired resolution of inflammation is due, at least in part, to impaired efferocytotic activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how the resolution of inflammation is linked to atherosclerosis and heart failure post myocardial infarct.
how macrophage clearance and resolution signaling are altered in atherosclerosis, and post MI.
how macrophage clearance of cell death in the heart, atherosclerosis, and other cardiovascular disorders may be modulated to promote resolution of inflammation and tissue repair.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the resolution of inflammation and tissue repair is not a passive process.

in advanced atheroma, defective effercocytosis is a hallmark feature of plaque instability and rupture, and in the infarcted myocardium, efferocytotic clearance is a key feature for resolution and repair.

the roles of eFFEROCYTOSIS IN ATHEROSCLEROSIS and Post MI are not yet fully understood, and further studies are warranted to elucidate the roles of phagocyte clearance in the context of these diseases and to identify potential therapeutic targets.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the clearance of dead cells and debris is critical to inflammation resolution and tissue repair.

efferocytosing macrophages are a major determinant of atherosclerosis plaque stability and that the same cells are also a key player in post MI cardiac remodeling, and thus, may be a therapeutic target for the prevention of heart failure.
in the heart, efferocytotic phagocytes are critical for tissue remodeling and repair, whereas in atherosclerosis, efferocytic macrophages are associated with inflammation and plaque instability.
The main takeaway from our work is that
in advanced atheroma, macrophages are defective in efferocytosing apoptotic cells.
the phagocytic clearance of cell debris is an essential process that is required for the maintenance of tissue homeostasis.
in contrast to the role of macrophage efferocytotic clearance in atherosclerosis, the role of efferocytic clearance of apoptotic cardiomyocytes and necrotic debris post MI is less well understood.
